description: GISIS is the International Maritime Organization's online system for the data that Member States and the Secretariat report under IMO conventions. Its Public Area, read on 28 September 2026, offers modules on ship and company particulars (the world fleet searchable by IMO number, and companies by IMO company number), maritime security information communicated under SOLAS chapter XI-2 and the ISPS Code (port facility security details), port reception facilities for ship-generated waste, marine casualties and incidents, piracy and armed robbery reports, recognized organizations, pollution prevention equipment and anti-fouling systems, the Global SAR plan on search and rescue services, the GMDSS, cargoes, facilitation data such as stowaway incidents, status of treaties and national maritime legislation. IMO keeps it to share the reported information among administrations, industry and the public. Coverage is global, at the level of individual ships, port facilities and reported events, with records spanning many years. Format and access: web search forms and tables; a free public account is required to open the Public Area, and a Member Area is reserved for administrations; no bulk download or open API is advertised. Licence: IMO terms of use; free. Caveats: content depends on what each Member State reports, so completeness varies, and casualty data follow the IMO reporting circulars. Simulation uses: port facility and ship inventories for maritime transport network models, historical casualty and piracy events for hazard and disruption analysis, and SAR service areas for emergency response planning. Related records: other maritime port and shipping records in the catalogue, such as port and vessel traffic data, can be joined through IMO numbers.
